instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead: peel the tough outer layers off the 3 lemongrass stalks and finely mince the bottom 4 inches of each. Mince 4 of the garlic cloves and the 2 shallots. Stir them in a bowl with 1/4 cup fish sauce, the 1/4 cup soy sauce, the 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 3 tbsp of the oil, the 2 tbsp honey and the 2 tbsp brown sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Put the 2 lb pork chops in a large zip top bag and pour in the marinade. Squeeze out the air, seal it, and rub the bag so every chop is coated. Put it in the fridge.

The same night, make the pickles. Peel and grate 1 carrot and half the daikon on the big holes of a box grater and pack them into a jar. Stir 1 cup water, the 1 cup rice vinegar and the 1 tsp salt together until the salt dissolves, pour it over the vegetables, put the lid on and refrigerate.
When you're ready to cook, heat the oven to 375°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on it.

Rinse the 2 cups broken rice until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/2 cups water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes.
Lift the chops out of the bag and lay them on the rack. Keep the marinade in the bag. Bake for 15 minutes.

Flip the chops and brush the tops with some of the marinade from the bag. Bake for another 12 minutes. Thicker chops, about 1 inch, need longer, so give those 10 to 15 minutes more on each side. Throw away any marinade that's left.
Switch the oven to broil and broil the chops for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges are dark and bubbling. Watch them closely. The honey burns fast.

You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest chop away from the bone. No thermometer? Cut into one next to the bone: it's done when the juices run clear and the meat is white with a faint blush of pink. Let the chops rest on the rack for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the nuoc cham. Squeeze the 2 limes into a bowl. You want about 3 tbsp juice. Add 3 tbsp fish sauce, the 3 tbsp sugar and 1/2 cup warm water and stir until the sugar dissolves. Mince the last garlic clove and stir it in.
Thinly slice the 2 chilies into a small bowl for the table.

Thinly slice the green onions and put them in a heatproof bowl. Heat 1/4 cup of the oil in a small pan over medium high for 1 to 2 minutes, until it shimmers. Pour it over the green onions. It will sizzle.
Cut the cucumber into thin slices and the 2 tomatoes into wedges.
Heat the last 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Crack in the 4 eggs and fry them for about 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the edges are crisp and the yolks are still runny.
Taste the nuoc cham. If it's flat, add a few drops more fish sauce.

Serve each plate with a mound of the broken rice, a pork chop, a fried egg, the cucumber, the tomato and some of the pickles, with the scallion oil spooned over the rice. Put the nuoc cham and the chilies on the side.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the pork chops and make the pickles the night before, or at least 3 hours ahead.
method_notes: Both marinate bone-in chops in fish sauce, oyster sauce, lemongrass, garlic, shallot and something sweet, and plate them on broken rice with cucumber, tomato, pickled carrot and daikon, a fried egg, scallion oil and nuoc cham. Cooking Therapy marinates for 3 hours or overnight with soy sauce, honey and brown sugar, bakes the chops on a rack at 375°F, flips and brushes them with marinade, and says grilling or pan frying works too. Tu David Phu adds ginger, five spice and marmalade, marinates for an hour, pan sears the chops, makes his scallion oil with pork fat and his nuoc cham with coconut water and lemon. This one follows the lead's marinade, oven and pickles, adds a short broil at the end for char, and uses a lime nuoc cham.
